guard: a wait's durable position survives a refused bind, and is deleted when the wait is genuinely over
why: The residual a review seat named and could not force. It reported the window honestly as
unresolved -- it had no chat stream to publish onto -- and the harness it needed already existed
in this suite, outside the files its brief allowed it to read.
The handler's own comment promises that BIND BEFORE ACK makes a crash between the two
recoverable. True of a CRASH, which never runs the cleanup at all. Not true of a `ctx.bind` that
FAILS -- and a bind is a journal append, which a journal refuses in ordinary operation (L5010,
RunSuperseded). The cleanup ran on every exit, so the durable holding this run's position on the
channel was deleted on the way out; the retry carries no recorded sequence, because recording it
is exactly what failed, so it created a fresh consumer at `deliver_policy: "new"` and found
NOTHING. The message sat on the stream permanently invisible to that run, with nothing red.
TWO DIRECTIONS, and they pull against each other, which is why both are mutated. Keeping the
consumer too eagerly leaks one per wait and re-opens the argument the handler settled when it
chose deletion over an inactivity threshold: a threshold could reap a LIVE wait's consumer while
its host was down, losing exactly the events the durable exists to hold. Deleting it too eagerly
is the defect above. The `over` flag is the whole distinction between them.
NOT GRADED HERE, and named rather than implied: the redelivery that actually consumes the kept
position is NATS's `ack_wait` (server default). It was measured end-to-end twice -- the retry
found the message again and re-bound a sequence -- and is not re-run in the gate, because a
45-second sleep buys a fact about the broker rather than about this code.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, and it is one config away rather than absent. Every mutation config in
this lane mutates a module its suite imports through a RELATIVE `../src/*.js` path, and no
command carries a build step -- all are bare `tsx` -- so the mutated bytes are the bytes the
suite loads. The suites in THIS directory nonetheless boot `@cotal-ai/core` and `@cotal-ai/lang`
through package specifiers that resolve to `dist`. So a future config that targets
`packages/lang/src` or `packages/core/src` under a `pnpm smoke:runtime-*` command would be VOID
ON ARRIVAL: the mutant would sit in `src` while the suite graded an untouched `dist`, and the
kill rate would measure module resolution rather than the guard. Either mutate the module the
suite imports relatively, or put a build between the mutation and the run.

mutations.name: every fire-read failure is read as 'the timer has not fired yet'
mutations.find:
if ((e as { code?: unknown })?.code === 10037) return null;
        throw e;
mutations.expectRed: the broker's refusal reaches the caller instead of reading as an unfired timer
mutations.cell: the broker's refusal reaches the caller instead of reading as an unfired timer
mutations.note: 10037 is the stream saying there is no message on that subject, which IS 'not yet'. Every other error is the broker, and reading those as 'not yet' is how a wait with a timeout outlives its own durable deadline in silence.
